Exercise: Seated Leg Tucks

Category:
strength

Exercise Type:
isolation

Force Type:
pull

Difficulty Level:
beginner

Movement Patterns:

- concentric
- eccentric
- bilateral

Primary Muscles:

- abdominals

Secondary Muscles:
None

Equipment:

- bodyweight

Fatigue Score:
2

Systemic Fatigue:
low

Stimulus To Fatigue Ratio:
0.8

Energy Requirement:
moderate

Recovery Time:
1 hours

Goals:

- core_strength_and_stability
- abdominal_muscle_definition

Contraindications:

- Individuals with lower back pain should avoid this exercise or perform it with caution.

Exercise Variations:
None

Substitution Options:

- exercise_name: Bicycle Crunches, equipment: body only
- exercise_name: Leg Raises, equipment: body only

Instructions:

- Sit on a bench with the legs stretched out in front of you slightly below parallel and your arms holding on to the sides of the bench. Your torso should be leaning backwards around a 45-degree angle from the bench. This will be your starting position.
- Bring the knees in toward you as you move your torso closer to them at the same time. Breathe out as you perform this movement.
- After a second pause, go back to the starting position as you inhale.
- Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
